clauses.requirement: Accelerated artificial weathering test (Table A6-1) shall use one of two parameter sets. TM1, black-standard thermometer, cycle No. 1 per EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry then 18 min water spray; irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) and 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm); black-standard temperature 65 ± 3 °C; relative humidity 50 ± 10 %. TM2, black-panel thermometer, cycle No. 4: 102 min dry then 18 min water spray; same irradiance values; black-panel temperature 63 ± 3 °C; relative humidity 50 ± 10 %. The two thermometers display different temperatures and results need not be identical; the sensor best correlating with the samples is recommended (e.g. black-panel for reflective material on aluminium substrate). Specimen preparation shall follow EN ISO 4892-2:2013; relocating samples in the xenon tester regularly (e.g. 4-8 times per test) is good lab practice. In case of dispute natural outdoor exposure results prevail. The ± tolerances are allowable fluctuations about the set value under equilibrium conditions, not permitted variation of the value.
The rear lamp, including its retro-reflector and lens, shall be subjected to the chemical testing specified in Annex 7 of UN R150.
The resistance to fuels shall be verified in accordance with Part 1 of Annex 7 (Resistance to fuels) of UN R150.

A test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol shall be used for the fuel resistance test of either a retro-reflective device or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking material, as specified in paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.

For a retro-reflective device (such as the rear retro-reflector), the outer surface, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture (70 vol. % n-heptane, 30 vol. % toluol); after about five minutes the surface shall be visually inspected and shall show no apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks are not objected to.

For a sample unit of retro-reflective marking material, a section not less than 300 mm long shall be immersed in the test mixture (70 vol. % n-heptane, 30 vol. % toluol) for one minute; after removal, the surface shall be wiped dry with a soft cloth and shall show no visible change that would reduce its effective performance.
Advance warning triangles shall be tested for resistance to fuels as specified in paragraph 2.1 of Annex 7 Part 1.

For advance warning triangles, the triangle and its protective cover shall be immersed separately in a tank containing 70 per cent n-heptane and 30 per cent toluene; after 60 seconds they shall be removed and drained of excess liquid; the triangle shall then be placed in its cover and the unit laid flat in a still atmosphere; when completely dried, the triangle shall not adhere to its cover and shall show no visually noticeable change on its surface or apparent detrimental modifications, although slight surface cracks may be tolerated.
